headline: Switzerland reaches World Cup quarterfinals for first time in 72 years after penalty shootout win
summary: Switzerland defeated Colombia 4-3 on penalties after a goalless draw, advancing to face defending champions Argentina. This marks their first quarterfinal appearance since 1954.
details: Switzerland secured a historic spot in the World Cup quarterfinals, beating Colombia 4-3 on penalties after a goalless draw on Wednesday. This achievement marks their first quarterfinal appearance since they hosted the World Cup in 1954, ending a 72-year wait.

The last-16 match, played outside the United States, saw both teams cancel each other out through 90 minutes of regular time and 30 minutes of extra time. Despite multiple substitutions and efforts, neither side managed to break the deadlock, leading to a tense penalty shootout.

Swiss goalkeeper Gregor Kobel emerged as a hero, brilliantly saving Cucho Hernandez's spot-kick. Ruben Vargas then stepped up to score the decisive penalty, sealing Switzerland's dramatic victory and their progression in the tournament.

Colombia, backed by thousands of passionate fans in Vancouver, had shown strong defensive form throughout the tournament, conceding only once in four games before this match. However, they ultimately fell short in the shootout.

Switzerland will now prepare to face defending champions Argentina in Kansas City on Saturday. Argentina secured their quarterfinal berth earlier by defeating Egypt 3-2 in Atlanta, setting up an exciting clash for the next stage of the competition.

headline: US strikes Iran again amid ceasefire, Tehran alleges breach of agreement
summary: US Central Command (CENTCOM) announced retaliatory strikes after Iran allegedly targeted commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz, a move Iran calls a ceasefire violation. This escalation occurs despite ongoing efforts for a permanent peace deal.
details: The US has launched strikes against Iran, citing Iranian attacks on commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz. US Central Command (CENTCOM) stated these were "powerful, continuous attacks" targeting Iran for "targeting innocent civilian mariners on an international waterway."

CENTCOM's X post claimed the strikes were in response to Iran's attacks on three commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz. It further described Iran's actions as "unjustified, dangerous, and a clear violation of the ceasefire."
Iranian media, citing Fars news agency, reported multiple explosions near Sirik and Qeshm areas in southern Iran. The specific source and cause of these explosions were not immediately known.

International media reported on Monday that at least three commercial ships were hit by "unknown objects" near the coast of Oman in the Strait of Hormuz. This critical waterway transports one-fifth of the world's total oil and gas.

The incident occurred despite an active ceasefire between the US and Iran and ongoing efforts to secure a permanent peace agreement. Both nations had signed a memorandum of understanding on June 18 to reach a final peace deal.

Iran's Foreign Ministry has accused the US of violating condition number 10 of their understanding. This alleged breach stems from the US revoking "temporary exemptions" on sanctions imposed on Iran's oil sales.
In a statement, Iran's Foreign Ministry asserted that the US violated the condition less than 20 days after signing the MoU. This, they claimed, proves the US administration cannot be trusted.
